text:
Dr B Townsend
Emergency Department
Newtown Children’s Hospital

10-04-10

Dear Dr Townsend,

R: Emma Johnson, aged 11

Thank you for urgently seeing Emma, who has exacerbated asthma
which triggered by viral URTI. Your urgent assessment would be highly
appreciated.

Emma has presented at my practice today with complaint of
deteriorated shortness of breath associated with wheezing over the
past two days. Emma has showed symptoms of viral URTI with loss of
appetite. On examination, inflamed throat and accessory muscles
usage were noticed but no focal signs. Emma’s PEFR has dropped to
140L/minute. Ventolin nebuliser had a minimal relief to her condition.

Over the past five months, Emma, who has a positive family history of
asthma, has complained of multiple episodes of viral URTI which
accompanied by nocturnal cough for which, paracetamol and fluids
were commenced. She was diagnosed with asthma. Salbutamol and
ventolin have failed to improve her symptoms; therefore, Becotide 200
2 puffs three times per day was prescribed and to continue using
ventolin. Emma has showed a good prognosis, her exercise-induced
asthma has improved and her PEFR has reached 340L/minute.

It would be appreciated if you could assess in Emma’s condition. Should
there be any queries, do not hesitate to contact me.
 
Yours sincerely,

Doctor
